hindi: अब इसके पश्चात् हम 'दीर्घञ्जीवितीय' नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter called Dīrghañjīvitīya ('On Long Life').
notes: The chapter title is formed from the opening words of verse 3, 'dīrghaṃ jīvitam' (long life), keeping the case ending of the first member (aluk compound) plus the suffix -īya.

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा था।
english: Thus indeed spoke the venerable Ātreya.
notes: 'iti ha sma āha' is a fixed formula of attribution; 'ha' and 'sma' are particles (sma marks past time).

hindi: दीर्घ जीवन की खोज करते हुए उग्र तपस्वी भरद्वाज, देवताओं के स्वामी इन्द्र को शरण देने योग्य जानकर, उनके पास गए।
english: Seeking a long life, Bharadvāja, a man of severe austerity, approached Indra, the lord of the immortals, having understood that he was the one fit to give refuge.
notes: 'ugratapāḥ' loses its visarga before the voiced 'b' of 'buddhvā'. 'buddhvā śaraṇyam' = knowing (him) to be the refuge.

hindi: क्योंकि ब्रह्मा ने जैसा आयुर्वेद कहा था, उसे पहले प्रजापति ने सम्पूर्ण रूप से ग्रहण किया; फिर उनसे दोनों अश्विनीकुमारों ने (ग्रहण किया)।
english: For Prajāpati first received Āyurveda (the science of life) in its entirety just as it had been proclaimed by Brahmā; then the Aśvins in turn (received it) from him.

text_flags.why: No word 'pajāpati' in Sanskrit; Prajāpati is the expected recipient in the lineage Brahmā > Prajāpati > Aśvins. A dropped 'r'. Metre unaffected (16 syllables either way).

notes: The verb 'jagrāha' must be supplied again (as a dual) for 'aśvinau'. 'yathāproktam' could also be read as an adverb ('exactly as it was taught'). 'tataḥ' = 'from him (Prajāpati)' or simply 'thereafter'.

hindi: अश्विनीकुमारों से भगवान् शक्र (इन्द्र) ने उसे सम्पूर्ण रूप से प्राप्त किया। ऋषियों द्वारा कहे जाने पर भरद्वाज इसलिए शक्र के पास गए।
english: From the Aśvins the venerable Śakra (Indra) received it in full. Bharadvāja, asked by the sages, therefore approached Śakra.
notes: 'kevalam' may qualify the science ('the whole of it') or be adverbial ('entirely'). 'ṛṣiproktaḥ' literally 'spoken to / told by the sages', i.e. requested or deputed by them (cf. verse 19). 'tasmāt' may mean 'therefore' or 'for that reason (since Śakra had it)'.

hindi: जब देहधारियों में रोग उत्पन्न हुए, जो उनके तप, उपवास, अध्ययन, ब्रह्मचर्य, व्रत और आयु में बाधा बन गए,
english: When diseases arose among embodied beings, becoming obstacles to their austerity, fasting, study, celibacy, vows and life,
notes: Sentence continues into verse 7. 'tapopavāsa' for tapas + upavāsa is the usual (irregular) compound form; not flagged. The genitive compound depends on 'vighnabhūtāḥ' (obstacles to ...); 'śarīriṇām' can be read with 'prādurbhūtāḥ' (arose among) or with the compound (the austerity etc. of embodied beings). 'brahmacarya-vrata' may also be taken as one item ('the vow of celibacy'); the whole compound may alternatively be read as a bahuvrīhi qualifying śarīriṇām.

hindi: तब प्राणियों के प्रति करुणा को आगे रखकर, पुण्य कर्म करने वाले महर्षि हिमालय के शुभ पार्श्व (ढलान) पर एकत्र हुए।
english: then, putting compassion for living beings foremost, great sages of virtuous deeds assembled on an auspicious slope of the Himālaya.
notes: Continues verse 6; the names of the sages follow in verses 8 to 13. 'pārśva' = side / flank (of the mountain).

hindi: अङ्गिरा, जमदग्नि, वसिष्ठ, कश्यप, भृगु, आत्रेय, गौतम, साङ्ख्य, पुलस्त्य, नारद, असित,

english: Agastya, Vāmadeva, Mārkaṇḍeya and Āśvalāyana, Pārikṣi, Ātreya the mendicant (Bhikṣu Ātreya), Bharadvāja, Kapiñjala,

hindi: विश्वामित्र और आश्मरथ्य, भार्गव च्यवन, अभिजित्, गार्ग्य, शाण्डिल्य और कौण्डिल्य, वार्क्षि, देवल और गालव,
english: Viśvāmitra and Āśmarathya, Cyavana the Bhārgava, Abhijit, Gārgya, Śāṇḍilya and Kauṇḍilya, Vārkṣi, Devala and Gālava,

hindi: साङ्कृत्य, बैजवापि, कुशिक, बादरायण, बडिश, शरलोमा, तथा काप्य और कात्यायन दोनों,

english: Kāṅkāyana, Kaikaśeya, Dhaumya, Mārīca and Kāśyapa, Śarkarākṣa, Hiraṇyākṣa, Lokākṣa, and also Paiṅgi,
notes: 'mārīcakāśyapau' is dual, so two persons (Mārīca and Kāśyapa), though the pair is sometimes understood as Mārīci Kāśyapa. The names in -akṣa are left unsplit since they are proper names (śarkara-akṣa etc.).

hindi: शौनक, शाकुनेय, मैत्रेय, मैमतायनि, वैखानस, वालखिल्य तथा अन्य महर्षि भी —
english: Śaunaka, Śākuneya, Maitreya, Maimatāyani, the Vaikhānasas, the Vālakhilyas, and likewise other great sages,
notes: Vaikhānasas and Vālakhilyas are groups (plural) of ascetics, not single persons.

hindi: जो ब्रह्मज्ञान, दम और नियम के भण्डार थे, और तप के तेज से ऐसे दीप्त थे जैसे आहुति पाती हुई अग्नियाँ —
english: repositories of the knowledge of Brahman, of self-restraint and of observances, blazing with the radiance of austerity like sacrificial fires receiving oblations,
notes: The edition notes the variant 'yamasya' in place of 'damasya' (giving the pair yama–niyama, 'restraints and observances'). 'tapasaḥ' is better taken with 'tejasā' ('the radiance of austerity'), since 'ca' closes the preceding list; it could also be read as a fourth item after 'nidhayaḥ'. 'brahmajñāna' may also be rendered 'sacred (Vedic) knowledge'.

hindi: वे वहाँ सुखपूर्वक बैठे और उन्होंने यह पुण्य चर्चा की — धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष का उत्तम मूल आरोग्य है।
english: Seated there at ease, they held this holy discussion: 'Health is the supreme root of dharma (righteousness), artha (wealth), kāma (pleasure) and mokṣa (liberation).
notes: The discussion (direct speech of the sages) runs from the second line of this verse through the first line of verse 17. Subject 'te' (they) refers back to the sages of verses 7 to 14.

hindi: रोग उस (आरोग्य) के, कल्याण के और जीवन के हरने वाले हैं। मनुष्यों के लिए यह बड़ी बाधा उत्पन्न हो गई है।
english: Diseases are the destroyers of it (health), of well-being and of life. This great obstacle has arisen for human beings.
notes: 'tasya' refers to 'ārogyam' (health) of verse 15. 'śreyas' = well-being / the higher good.

hindi: "उनकी शान्ति का क्या उपाय हो?" — ऐसा कहकर वे ध्यान में स्थित हो गए। तब उन्होंने ध्यान-चक्षु से शक्र (इन्द्र) को शरण के रूप में देखा।
english: What could be the means of curing them?' Having said this, they entered into meditation. Then, with the eye of meditation, they saw Śakra as their refuge.
notes: 'śamopāya' before 'ity' is 'śamopāyaḥ' (visarga dropped before a vowel after -a). 'teṣām' = of the diseases. 'śama' literally 'pacification, allaying'. 'śaraṇaṃ śakram' = Śakra as refuge (predicative).

hindi: "वे अमरों के स्वामी (इन्द्र) शान्ति का उपाय यथावत् बताएँगे। शचीपति से पूछने के लिए सहस्राक्ष (इन्द्र) के भवन में कौन जाए?"
english: 'He, the lord of the immortals, will tell (us) the means of cure properly. Who should go to the abode of the thousand-eyed one to ask the husband of Śacī?'
notes: Thought / speech of the sages. Sahasrākṣa (thousand-eyed), Śacīpati (husband of Śacī), amaraprabhu are all epithets of Indra.

hindi: "इस कार्य के लिए मुझे नियुक्त किया जाए" — यह वचन भरद्वाज ने सबसे पहले कहा; इसलिए ऋषियों ने उन्हें नियुक्त किया।
english: 'Let me be appointed to this task' — these words Bharadvāja spoke first; therefore he was appointed by the sages.
notes: 'arthe ... atra' = 'for this purpose/task here'. 'prathamaṃ vacaḥ' = he was the first to speak (before the other sages). 'niyujyeyam' is a non-classical (ārṣa) form: passive stem with active ending; classical Sanskrit would have 'niyujyeya'.

hindi: शक्र के भवन में जाकर उन्होंने देवताओं और ऋषियों के समूहों के बीच स्थित, प्रज्वलित अग्नि के समान दीप्तिमान, बल (असुर) का वध करने वाले (इन्द्र) को देखा।
english: Having gone to Śakra's abode, he saw the slayer of Bala (Indra), amid hosts of gods and sages, blazing like fire.
notes: 'surarṣi' may be 'gods and sages' (dvandva) or 'divine sages' (karmadhāraya). Bala is a demon slain by Indra.

hindi: उस बुद्धिमान् (भरद्वाज) ने पास जाकर, विजय के आशीर्वादों से देवताओं के स्वामी का अभिनन्दन करके, विनयपूर्वक ऋषियों का उत्तम वचन कहा —
english: Having approached and greeted the lord of the gods with blessings of victory, the wise one humbly conveyed the excellent message of the sages:

text_flags.why: 'ṛsīṇām' has dental s; the genitive plural of ṛṣi is 'ṛṣīṇām' (retroflex ṣ, as elsewhere in the chunk: ṛṣibhiḥ, ṛṣibhyaḥ). Data-entry typo; the Devanagari line has the same error.

notes: 'vinayāt' (ablative) = out of humility / humbly. The message itself is verse 22.

hindi: "समस्त प्राणियों को भयभीत करने वाले रोग उत्पन्न हो गए हैं; अतः हे अमरों के स्वामी, मुझे उनकी शान्ति का उपाय यथावत् बताइए।"
english: 'Diseases have arisen that terrify all living beings; therefore, O lord of the immortals, tell me properly the means of curing them.'
notes: 'tat' may be the conjunction 'therefore' or a pronoun qualifying the means ('that means'). 'bhayaṅkara' keeps the internal m (bhayam-kara).

hindi: उस परम ऋषि की बुद्धि को विशाल जानकर भगवान् शतक्रतु (इन्द्र) ने उन्हें थोड़े शब्दों में आयुर्वेद का उपदेश दिया।
english: Recognising the vast intellect of that supreme sage, the venerable Śatakratu (Indra) taught him Āyurveda in few words.
notes: 'tasmai' and 'paramarṣaye' both refer to Bharadvāja. 'matiṃ buddhvā vipulām' = understanding (his) intellect to be vast (predicative), which is why few words sufficed.

english: (that Āyurveda) which is the knowledge of cause, sign (symptom) and remedy, the supreme resort of the healthy and the sick, threefold in its aphorisms (trisūtra), eternal and holy, which the Grandfather (Brahmā) had understood.
notes: All adjectives agree with 'āyurvedam' of verse 23 (masc. acc. sg.); 'yam' also refers to it. 'trisūtra' = having three basic topics/aphorisms, i.e. cause, sign and remedy. 'parāyaṇa' = highest resort / support / means; 'svasthāturaparāyaṇa' may also mean 'devoted to (the good of) the healthy and the sick'.

english: That sage of great intellect, with his mind fixed on it, quickly and properly understood the whole of Āyurveda, which is boundless in extent and has three divisions (triskandha).
notes: 'anantapāra' literally 'whose far shore is endless'. 'triskandha' (three divisions/trunks) is generally taken as the same triad as 'trisūtra' (cause, sign, remedy). 'tanmanāḥ' loses visarga before 'm'.

hindi: तब मैत्री-परायण पुनर्वसु ने समस्त प्राणियों पर अनुकम्पा के कारण पुण्य आयुर्वेद छह शिष्यों को प्रदान किया।
english: Then Punarvasu, devoted to friendliness, out of compassion for all beings gave the holy Āyurveda (the science of life) to his six disciples.
notes: Punarvasu is Ātreya (cf. unit 33 'ātreyam'). 'puṇyam' agrees with āyurvedam (m. acc. sg.).

hindi: अग्निवेश, भेल, जतूकर्ण, पराशर, हारीत और क्षारपाणि ने उन मुनि के उस वचन (उपदेश) को ग्रहण किया।
english: Agniveśa, Bhela, Jatūkarṇa, Parāśara, Hārīta and Kṣārapāṇi received that teaching of the sage.
notes: The edition notes the variant 'bheḍaśca' (Bheḍa) for 'bhelaśca'; Bhela and Bheḍa are two spellings of the same name.

hindi: इसमें (शिष्यों की) बुद्धि की विशेषता थी, मुनि के उपदेश में कोई भेद नहीं था; इसी कारण अग्निवेश सबसे पहले तन्त्र (शास्त्र-ग्रन्थ) के रचयिता हुए।
english: The distinction there lay in intellect, not in any difference in the sage's teaching; that is why Agniveśa became the first author of a treatise (tantra).
notes: 'buddher viśeṣaḥ' is understood as Agniveśa's superior intellect (the teaching given to all six was the same). 'prathamam' may also be read adjectivally with 'tantrasya' ('author of the first treatise').

hindi: तब भेल आदि ने भी अपना-अपना तन्त्र रचा, और उन मेधावी शिष्यों ने अपनी रचनाएँ ऋषि-समूह सहित आत्रेय को सुनाईं।
english: Then Bhela and the others each composed his own treatise, and those highly intelligent ones recited their compositions to Ātreya together with the assembly of sages.
notes: 'kṛtāni ca' (the works made) is the object of 'śrāvayām āsuḥ', with 'ātreyam' as the person made to hear (double accusative with the causative).
lines_iast: atha bhelādayaścakruḥ svaṃ svaṃ tantraṃ kṛtāni ca
lines_deva: अथ भेलादयश्चक्रुः स्वं स्वं तन्त्रं कृतानि च

hindi: पुण्यकर्मा (शिष्यों) द्वारा विषयों की सूत्र-रूप रचना सुनकर वे ऋषि अत्यन्त प्रसन्न हुए और 'यथावत् सूत्रित किया गया है' ऐसा कहकर उन्होंने उसका अनुमोदन किया।
english: Having heard the systematic composition of the subjects by those of meritorious deeds, the sages, delighted, approved it, saying: "It has been properly composed."

text_flags.why: Sandhi of prahṛṣṭāḥ + te before avagraha ('numenire = anumenire) requires 'te', giving 'prahṛṣṭāste 'numenire'; 'sta' with avagraha is not a valid form. Likely data-entry typo (Devanagari shows the same).

notes: 'puṇyakarmaṇām' is taken as the agent of 'sūtraṇam' (the composition by those of meritorious deeds, i.e. the disciples); it could alternatively qualify 'arthānām'.

hindi: सब प्राणियों का हित चाहने वाले उन सभी (ऋषियों) ने उनकी प्रशंसा की और एक साथ ऊँचे स्वर में कहा — 'साधु! (यह) प्राणियों पर अनुकम्पा है।'
english: All of them, wishing the welfare of all beings, praised them and together said loudly: "Well done! (This is) compassion for living beings."
notes: 'sarva' = sarve (final -e becomes -a before a vowel, eva). The exclamation may also be construed '(Your) compassion for beings is good (sādhu).' 'sarvabhūtahitaiṣiṇaḥ' may be acc. pl. agreeing with 'tān' (praised them, who wished the welfare of all beings) rather than nom. pl. with 'sarve'.

hindi: स्वर्ग में स्थित देवर्षियों ने देवताओं सहित उन परम ऋषियों का वह पुण्य शब्द सुना, और सुनकर वे अत्यन्त प्रसन्न हुए।
english: The divine sages stationed in heaven, together with the gods, heard that holy utterance of the supreme sages, and having heard it they rejoiced greatly.

text_flags.why: Genitive plural of ṛṣi ends in -īṇām with long ā; short 'ṇaṃ' is ungrammatical and a likely data-entry typo (Devanagari shows the same). The metre cannot decide it: the syllable is heavy either way because of the anusvāra.

notes: 'paramarṣīṇām' could depend on 'śabdam' (the sound of the supreme sages) — taken so here.
lines_iast: taṃ puṇyaṃ śuśruvuḥ śabdaṃ divi devarṣayaḥ sthitāḥ
lines_deva: तं पुण्यं शुश्रुवुः शब्दं दिवि देवर्षयः स्थिताः

words.gram: ppp. caus. ud-√īr, m. nom. sg.

hindi: आकाश में प्राणियों द्वारा हर्ष से उच्चारित 'अहो, साधु!' के स्निग्ध और गम्भीर घोष ने तीनों लोकों को गुंजा दिया।
english: The cry "Ah, well done!", smooth and deep, raised in the sky by beings out of joy, made the three worlds resound.
notes: Variant noted by the edition: '-nādayat' (anvanādayat, 'made resound/echo', caus. of √nad) for 'anvavādayat'; the sense is nearly the same. 'bhūtaiḥ' may mean spirits/celestial beings rather than creatures generally. The variant anvanādayat (caus. of √nad) gives the more natural sense 'made resound'; anvavādayat as a causative of anu-√vad is possible but unusual.

words.gram: ppp. caus. ud-√mīl, f. nom. pl.

hindi: मंगलकारी वायु बहने लगी, सभी दिशाएँ प्रकाश से जगमगा उठीं, और जल-सहित पुष्पों की दिव्य वर्षाएँ होने लगीं।
english: An auspicious wind blew, all the directions were lit up with radiance, and heavenly showers of flowers fell, accompanied by water.
notes: 'sajalāḥ' (with water) qualifies 'kusumavṛṣṭayaḥ': flower-showers mixed with (fragrant) water/rain.

hindi: तब अग्निवेश आदि (शिष्यों) में ज्ञान की देवियाँ प्रविष्ट हुईं — बुद्धि, सिद्धि, स्मृति, मेधा, धृति, कीर्ति, क्षमा और दया।
english: Then the deities of knowledge entered Agniveśa and the others headed by him: Intellect, Accomplishment, Memory, Retentive intelligence (medhā), Fortitude, Fame, Forbearance and Compassion.
notes: 'kṣamādayā' is two words, kṣamā and dayā, written without a space (no sandhi change; Devanagari likewise joined). It is not 'kṣamā-ādayaḥ' ('forbearance etc.'), which would be masculine plural and break the list of feminine deities.
lines_iast: buddhiḥ siddhiḥ smṛtirmedhā dhṛtiḥ kīrtiḥ kṣamādayā
lines_deva: बुद्धिः सिद्धिः स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः कीर्तिः क्षमादया

hindi: और परम ऋषियों द्वारा अनुमोदित इनके वे तन्त्र प्राणि-समूहों के कल्याण के लिए पृथ्वी पर प्रतिष्ठित हो गए।
english: And those treatises of theirs, approved by the supreme sages, gained a firm standing on earth for the welfare of the multitudes of beings.
notes: Variant noted by the edition: 'bhāvāya' for 'bhavāya' (sense: for the well-being/prosperity). 'bhava' could also mean 'existence', but 'welfare/prosperity' fits the context. 'eṣām' may also be taken with 'paramarṣibhiḥ' (approved by these supreme sages).

hindi: हितकर और अहितकर, सुखी और दुःखी आयु, उस आयु के लिए क्या हितकर और क्या अहितकर है, उसका मान (परिमाण) और स्वयं वह आयु — ये जहाँ कहे गए हों, वह आयुर्वेद कहलाता है।
english: That in which beneficial and harmful life, happy and unhappy life, what is wholesome and unwholesome for that life, its measure, and life itself are stated, is called Āyurveda.

text_flags.why: 'dukham' lacks the visarga of duḥkham; with duḥ the 7th syllable of the odd pāda becomes heavy (regular pathyā pattern), so the metre supports duḥkham. Likely data-entry typo (Devanagari also shows दुखम्).

notes: 'āyuḥ' is qualified by hitāhitam, sukham, duḥkham (four kinds of life: hita, ahita, sukha, duḥkha). The first 'hitāhitam' qualifies āyuḥ; the second ('tasya hitāhitam') means what is wholesome and unwholesome for it. 'mānam' = the measure (span) of life. Masculine 'saḥ' agrees with 'āyurvedaḥ'.
lines_iast: mānaṃ ca tacca yatroktamāyurvedaḥ sa ucyate
lines_deva: मानं च तच्च यत्रोक्तमायुर्वेदः स उच्यते

words.gloss: union of body, senses, mind, self
words.gram: m. nom. sg.; dvandva within tat-puruṣa

hindi: शरीर, इन्द्रिय, सत्त्व (मन) और आत्मा का संयोग आयु है; पर्यायवाची शब्दों से उसे धारि, जीवित, नित्यग और अनुबन्ध कहा जाता है।
english: The union of body, sense faculties, mind (sattva) and self is life (āyus); by synonyms life is called dhāri (sustaining), jīvita (living), nityaga (ever-moving) and anubandha (continuity).
notes: Syntax: the union (saṃyoga) is the definition of āyus; dhāri, jīvitam, nityagaḥ, anubandhaḥ are the synonyms. 'nityaga' is variously explained as 'constantly going (moving on)' or 'ever-present'; 'anubandha' as 'continuity (linking successive moments)'.

hindi: उस आयु का वेद (आयुर्वेद) वेदज्ञों द्वारा सबसे अधिक पुण्यकारी माना गया है; (अब) वह कहा जाएगा जो मनुष्यों के लिए दोनों लोकों में हितकर है।
english: The Veda (science) of that life is regarded by the knowers of the Vedas as the most holy; that which is beneficial to human beings in both worlds will now be expounded.
notes: 'yat ... hitam' is neuter while 'vedaḥ' is masculine, so 'yat' is best taken as 'that which (is beneficial)', the content to be taught, rather than as a relative to vedaḥ. 'lokayoḥ ubhayoḥ' may be locative or genitive dual ('of both worlds'); this world and the next are meant. 'vakṣyate' form is middle/passive future of √vac.

hindi: सामान्य सदा सभी भावों (पदार्थों) की वृद्धि का कारण है और विशेष ह्रास का कारण; किन्तु प्रवृत्ति (प्रयोग) दोनों की होती है।
english: Commonality (sāmānya) is always the cause of increase of all entities, and distinctiveness (viśeṣa) the cause of decrease; but the operation (pravṛtti) belongs to both.
notes: 'pravṛttir ubhayasya tu' is terse: commentators take it as 'both are operative (simultaneously / in application)', i.e. both principles are applied in practice; some read it as 'the application (of treatment) is of both'. The literal rendering is kept.

hindi: सामान्य एकत्व उत्पन्न करता है, जबकि विशेष पृथक्त्व उत्पन्न करता है; सामान्य वस्तुतः तुल्य-अर्थता (समानता) है, और विशेष उसका विपरीत है।
english: Commonality produces oneness, while distinctiveness produces separateness; commonality is indeed sameness of purpose (tulyārthatā), and distinctiveness is its opposite.
notes: 'tulyārthatā' is understood as 'having the same effect/purpose' (e.g. substances acting alike); 'artha' could also mean 'object' or 'meaning'.

hindi: सत्त्व (मन), आत्मा और शरीर — ये तीनों त्रिदण्ड (तिपाई) के समान हैं; इनके संयोग से लोक टिका रहता है और उसी में सब कुछ प्रतिष्ठित है।
english: Mind (sattva), self and body: this triad is like a tripod. The world (of living beings) stands through their union, and in that everything is established.
notes: 'tridaṇḍa' = three staves tied together (tripod). 'tatra' may refer to the union (saṃyoga) or to the living being (loka).

words.gram: ppp. caus. sam-pra-√kāś, m. nom. sg.

hindi: वही (संयोग) पुरुष है, वही चेतन है और वही इस वेद का अधिकरण (विषय) माना गया है; उसी के लिए यह वेद प्रकाशित किया गया है।
english: That (union) is the person (puruṣa); it is the sentient being, and it is regarded as the subject (adhikaraṇa) of this Veda; for its sake indeed this Veda has been revealed.
notes: 'saḥ pumān' (masculine) refers back to the union of mind, self and body; 'tat cetanam' and 'tat adhikaraṇam' are neuter, referring to the same. 'adhikaraṇa' may be rendered 'locus / object of treatment'.
lines_deva: वेदस्यास्य तदर्थं हि वेदो ऽयं संप्रकाशितः

hindi: ख (आकाश) आदि (पाँच भूत), आत्मा, मन, काल और दिशाएँ — यह द्रव्यों का संग्रह है। इन्द्रिय-युक्त द्रव्य चेतन है और इन्द्रिय-रहित अचेतन।
english: The (five elements) beginning with kha (space), the self, mind, time and the directions: this is the summary of substances (dravya). Substance possessing sense faculties is sentient; that without sense faculties is non-sentient.
notes: 'khādīni' = the five bhūtas: kha/ākāśa, vāyu, agni, jala, pṛthivī (the list is implied, not stated).

hindi: इन्द्रिय-विषयों (अर्थों) सहित गुरु आदि, बुद्धि, प्रयत्न-पर्यन्त (गुण) और पर आदि — ये गुण कहे गए हैं। प्रयत्न से आरम्भ होने वाली चेष्टा को कर्म कहा जाता है।
english: Together with the sense-objects (artha), those beginning with guru (heavy), intellect (buddhi) and those ending with effort (prayatna), and those beginning with para (priority): these are declared to be the qualities (guṇa). Action (karma) is called movement (ceṣṭita) initiated by effort.
notes: Very compressed list. 'sārthāḥ' = with the sense-objects (sound etc.); 'gurvādayaḥ' = the twenty qualities beginning with heavy; 'buddhiḥ prayatnāntāḥ' is usually read as 'buddhi and the (psychic qualities) ending with prayatna' (icchā, dveṣa, sukha, duḥkha, prayatna); 'parādayaḥ' = para, apara, yukti, etc. Whether 'prayatnāntāḥ' is a separate group or qualifies buddhi is construed differently; the translation keeps it neutral. 'prayatnādi' (n. sg.) qualifies 'karma' (action preceded by effort).

hindi: पृथ्वी आदि का अपने गुणों के साथ अपृथक्-भाव (अविभाज्य सम्बन्ध) समवाय माना गया है। वह नित्य है, क्योंकि जहाँ द्रव्य है वहाँ गुण अनियत (अनुपस्थित) नहीं होता।
english: Inherence (samavāya) is held to be the inseparable existence of earth and the rest with their qualities. It is eternal, for wherever there is a substance, there quality is not absent (is invariably present).
notes: 'aniyataḥ' literally 'not fixed / not bound'; the sense is that a quality is never lacking where a substance is.
lines_iast: sa nityo yatra hi dravyaṃ na tatrāniyato guṇaḥ
lines_deva: स नित्यो यत्र हि द्रव्यं न तत्रानियतो गुणः

hindi: जिसमें कर्म और गुण आश्रित रहते हैं और जो समवायी कारण है, वह द्रव्य है; गुण तो समवायी, चेष्टा-रहित कारण है।
english: That in which actions and qualities reside, and which is the inherent cause, is substance (dravya). Quality (guṇa), on the other hand, is an inhering cause that is devoid of movement.
notes: 'samavāyī tu niśceṣṭaḥ kāraṇaṃ guṇaḥ': quality inheres (in substance) and is a cause, but has no motion. 'samavāyī' might alternatively mean 'inhering (in substance)' rather than 'inherent cause'; both senses are close.
lines_iast: taddravyaṃ samavāyī tu niśceṣṭaḥ kāraṇaṃ guṇaḥ
lines_deva: तद्द्रव्यं समवायी तु निश्चेष्टः कारणं गुणः

words.gloss: of what is to be done

hindi: संयोग और विभाग में कारण, द्रव्य में आश्रित, और करने योग्य (कार्य) की क्रिया — यह कर्म है; कर्म किसी अन्य की अपेक्षा नहीं रखता।
english: That which is the cause of conjunction and disjunction, residing in substance, the performance of what is to be done, is action (karma); action does not depend on anything else.
notes: Line 1 is a description of karma, the subject named in line 2. 'dravyam āśritam': 'āśrita' with accusative = resting on substance. 'karma nānyad apekṣate' is understood (commentary) as: action needs nothing else to produce conjunction/disjunction; the literal sense is kept.
lines_iast: saṃyoge ca vibhāge ca kāraṇaṃ dravyamāśritam
lines_deva: संयोगे च विभागे च कारणं द्रव्यमाश्रितम्

hindi: इस प्रकार कारण कह दिया गया। यहाँ कार्य धातुसाम्य (धातुओं की समता) कहा जाता है, और धातुसाम्य की क्रिया (उसे स्थापित करना) इस तन्त्र का प्रयोजन कही गई है।
english: Thus the cause has been stated. Here the effect is said to be equilibrium of the dhātus (constituents), and the bringing about of equilibrium of the dhātus is declared to be the purpose of this treatise.
notes: 'kāraṇam' refers to the six causal categories (sāmānya, viśeṣa, guṇa, dravya, karma, samavāya) just described. 'kāryam' may also be rendered 'what is to be achieved'.

hindi: काल, बुद्धि और इन्द्रियार्थों (इन्द्रियों के विषयों) का मिथ्या, अ- (हीन) और अति योग — यह दो आश्रयों (शरीर और मन) वाले रोगों के कारणों का त्रिविध संग्रह है।
english: Wrong, deficient (non-) and excessive conjunction (yoga) of time, intellect and sense-objects is the threefold summary of the causes of diseases, which have two seats.
notes: 'yogo mithyā na cāti ca' = mithyā-yoga, a-yoga (na) and ati-yoga. 'indriyārtha' = the objects of the senses (some take it as senses and their objects). The two seats are body and mind (cf. unit 55).
lines_iast: kālabuddhīndriyārthānāṃ yogo mithyā na cāti ca
lines_deva: कालबुद्धीन्द्रियार्थानां योगो मिथ्या न चाति च

hindi: शरीर और सत्त्व नामक (मन) रोगों के आश्रय माने गए हैं, और उसी प्रकार सुखों (आरोग्य) के भी; किन्तु सम योग सुखों का कारण है।
english: The body and that which is called sattva (mind) are held to be the seat of diseases, and likewise of states of well-being (sukha); but balanced conjunction is the cause of well-being.
notes: 'sukha' here stands for health (the opposite of vyādhi). 'samaḥ yogaḥ' = proper (balanced) conjunction of time, intellect and sense-objects, contrasting with the three faulty kinds in unit 54.
lines_iast: tathā sukhānāṃ yogastu sukhānāṃ kāraṇaṃ samaḥ
lines_deva: तथा सुखानां योगस्तु सुखानां कारणं समः

hindi: परम आत्मा तो निर्विकार है; वह सत्त्व (मन), भूतों, गुणों और इन्द्रियों के साथ मिलकर चेतना का कारण है; वह नित्य है, द्रष्टा है, क्योंकि वह क्रियाओं को देखता है।
english: The supreme self, however, is unchanging; together with mind, the elements, the qualities and the senses it is the cause of consciousness. It is eternal and the seer, for it witnesses actions.
notes: The instrumental 'sattvabhūtaguṇendriyaiḥ' is taken with 'caitanye kāraṇam' (the self causes consciousness in association with these); it could also be construed with 'nirvikāraḥ' ('unaffected by mind, elements...'), which is less usual. 'caitanye' is a locative of purpose ('cause in regard to consciousness'). 'guṇa' may mean the qualities of the elements (sense-objects).
lines_iast: caitanye kāraṇaṃ nityo draṣṭā paśyati hi kriyāḥ
lines_deva: चैतन्ये कारणं नित्यो द्रष्टा पश्यति हि क्रियाः

hindi: वायु (वात), पित्त और कफ — यह शारीरिक दोषों का संग्रह कहा गया है; और मानसिक (दोष-संग्रह) रज तथा तम बताया गया है।
english: Vāyu (Vāta), Pitta and Kapha are stated to be the group of bodily doṣas; the mental group, on the other hand, is declared to be rajas and tamas.
notes: 'tama eva': tamaḥ before a vowel loses the visarga (tamas + eva → tama eva).
lines_iast: mānasaḥ punaruddiṣṭo rajaśca tama eva ca
lines_deva: मानसः पुनरुद्दिष्टो रजश्च तम एव च

words.gloss: based on the divine and on reasoning
words.gram: n. inst. pl.; bahuvrīhi with dvandva

words.gloss: by knowledge, understanding, fortitude, memory, concentration

hindi: पहला (शारीरिक दोष) दैवव्यपाश्रय और युक्तिव्यपाश्रय औषधियों से शान्त होता है; मानसिक (दोष) ज्ञान, विज्ञान, धैर्य, स्मृति और समाधि से।
english: The former (the bodily group) is pacified by remedies based on the divine (daiva) and on rational planning (yukti); the mental, by knowledge, specific understanding (vijñāna), fortitude, memory and concentration (samādhi).
notes: 'pūrvaḥ' and 'mānasaḥ' refer to the bodily and mental doṣa-groups of unit 57. 'jñāna' (knowledge, e.g. of the self) vs 'vijñāna' (specific/scriptural understanding) are distinguished differently by commentators.

hindi: वायु (मारुत) रूक्ष, शीत, लघु, सूक्ष्म, चल, विशद और खर है; वह इनके विपरीत गुणों वाले द्रव्यों से भली-भाँति शान्त हो जाता है।
english: Vāta (here called māruta, wind) is rough, cold, light, subtle, mobile, clear (non-slimy) and coarse; it is thoroughly pacified by substances having the opposite qualities.
notes: The adjectives in line 1 are masculine nominative agreeing with mārutaḥ. viśada: 'clear, non-slimy', the opposite of picchila (slimy).
lines_iast: rūkṣaḥ śīto laghuḥ sūkṣmaścalo 'tha viśadaḥ kharaḥ
lines_deva: रूक्षः शीतो लघुः सूक्ष्मश्चलो ऽथ विशदः खरः

hindi: पित्त स्नेहयुक्त (सस्नेह), उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, द्रव, अम्ल, सर और कटु है; यह विपरीत गुणों वाले द्रव्यों से शीघ्र शान्त हो जाता है।
english: Pitta is unctuous (sa-sneha, literally 'with oiliness'), hot, sharp, liquid, sour, flowing and pungent; it is quickly pacified by substances having the opposite qualities.
notes: sa-sneha literally 'with unctuousness'; commentators take sa- as 'slightly' (īṣat). sara: 'flowing / mobile', also 'laxative'.
lines_iast: sasnehamuṣṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca dravamamlaṃ saraṃ kaṭu
lines_deva: सस्नेहमुष्णं तीक्ष्णं च द्रवमम्लं सरं कटु

words.gloss: heavy, cold, soft, unctuous, sweet, stable, slimy

hindi: श्लेष्मा (कफ) के गुरु, शीत, मृदु, स्निग्ध, मधुर, स्थिर और पिच्छिल गुण विपरीत गुणों से शान्त हो जाते हैं।
english: The qualities of Kapha (śleṣman) — heavy, cold, soft, unctuous, sweet, stable and slimy — are pacified by the opposite qualities.
notes: śleṣman is masculine (n-stem); śleṣmaṇaḥ is gen. sg. Here viparīta-guṇaiḥ is best read as 'by opposite qualities' (with dravyaiḥ understood from the preceding verses).

words.gram: n. inst. pl.; tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: जो विकार साध्य माने गए हैं, वे विपरीत गुणों वाली तथा देश, मात्रा और काल का ध्यान रखकर दी गई औषधियों से निवृत्त हो जाते हैं।
english: Disorders regarded as curable are removed by medicines having the opposite qualities, administered with due regard to place, dose and time.
notes: deśa may mean the locality/habitat or the patient's body (site); left as 'place'. upapādita: 'applied, administered, made suitable'.

hindi: किन्तु असाध्य रोगों की चिकित्सा का उपदेश नहीं किया जाता। और इसके आगे प्रत्येक द्रव्य के अनुसार उसके गुण और कर्म (विस्तार से) बताए जाएँगे।
english: But treatment is not taught for incurable diseases. Further, from here on, the qualities and actions (guṇa and karma) will be stated substance by substance.
notes: vakṣyate is singular with plural subject guṇakarmāṇi; it may be taken impersonally ('it will be told') — a common usage. bhūyaḥ may also mean 'in more detail'.

hindi: रसना (जिह्वा) का विषय रस है; उसका आधारभूत द्रव्य जल और पृथ्वी है; और उसकी उत्पत्ति तथा विशेषता (भेद) में आकाश आदि तीन (महाभूत) कारण हैं।
english: Taste (rasa) is the object of the tongue; its material basis (dravya) is water and earth; and in its production and in its differentiation the three beginning with ether are the causes.
notes: kha-ādayaḥ trayaḥ: 'the three beginning with kha (ether)', i.e. presumably ether, air and fire (the remaining elements besides water and earth); the text does not name them. nirvṛtti 'production, manifestation'; viśeṣa 'specific distinction (into different tastes)'. Some take both terms together as 'in its manifestation and specific variation'.
lines_iast: nirvṛttau ca viśeṣe ca pratyayāḥ khādayastrayaḥ
lines_deva: निर्वृत्तौ च विशेषे च प्रत्ययाः खादयस्त्रयः

hindi: मधुर, अम्ल, लवण, कटु, तिक्त और कषाय — यह छह का समूह रसों का संग्रह माना गया है।
english: Sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and astringent — this group of six is known as the summary of the tastes.
lines_deva: स्वादुरम्लो ऽथ लवणः कटुकस्तिक्त एव च
कषायश्चेति षट्को ऽयं रसानां संग्रहः स्मृतः

hindi: मधुर, अम्ल और लवण रस वायु को जीतते हैं; कषाय, मधुर और तिक्त रस पित्त को; तथा कषाय, कटु और तिक्त रस श्लेष्मा (कफ) को जीतते (शान्त करते) हैं।
english: Sweet, sour and salty (tastes) overcome Vāta; astringent, sweet and bitter overcome Pitta; astringent, pungent and bitter overcome Kapha.
notes: jayanti is shared by all three subject groups. vāyu = Vāta.

hindi: कटु, अम्ल और लवण रस पित्त को; मधुर, अम्ल और लवण रस कफ को; और कटु, तिक्त तथा कषाय रस समीरण (वायु) को कुपित करते हैं।
english: Pungent, sour and salty (tastes) aggravate Pitta; sweet, sour and salty aggravate Kapha; and pungent, bitter and astringent aggravate samīraṇa (Vāta).

text_flags.why: svādu 'sweet' requires long ā; cf. svādvamla- in verse 66 of this chunk. Metre is unaffected (the syllable is heavy by position), so this is a data-entry slip.

notes: Printed in parentheses in the edition: an interpolated or alternative verse. It states the converse of verse 66 (which tastes aggravate each doṣa).

hindi: कोई द्रव्य दोषों का शमन करने वाला है, कोई धातुओं को दूषित करने वाला है, और कोई स्वस्थवृत्त (स्वास्थ्य-रक्षा) में उपयोगी माना गया है; इस प्रकार द्रव्य तीन प्रकार का कहा जाता है।
english: Some substance pacifies the doṣas, some vitiates the dhātus (tissues), and some is regarded as suited to maintaining health; thus substance (dravya) is said to be threefold.
notes: svastha-vṛtti: 'the regimen of the healthy'; 'matam' here implies 'considered (beneficial/suitable)'.

hindi: वह द्रव्य फिर तीन प्रकार का कहा गया है — जांगम (प्राणिज), औद्भिद (वनस्पतिज) और पार्थिव (खनिज)। मधु, गोरस (दूध आदि), पित्त, वसा, मज्जा, रक्त, मांस —
english: That (substance) is again declared to be threefold: animal (jaṅgama), plant (audbhida) and earthly (pārthiva). Honeys, cow products (milk etc.), bile, fat, marrow, blood, flesh —
notes: Line 2 begins a list that continues into verse 69 (ending 'are used from animals'). go-rasa: 'products of the cow', i.e. milk, curd, ghee etc. majjan is masculine (n-stem), nom. majjā. The edition writes majjā 'sṛk with avagraha: majjā + asṛk.
lines_deva: मधूनि गोरसाः पित्तं वसा मज्जा ऽसृगामिषम्

words.gloss: feces, urine, skin, semen, bone, sinew, horn, nails

hindi: मल, मूत्र, चर्म, शुक्र, अस्थि, स्नायु, सींग, नख, खुर, केश, लोम और रोचना — ये जांगम (प्राणियों) से (प्राप्त करके) प्रयोग किए जाते हैं।
english: Feces, urine, skin, semen, bone, sinew, horn, nails, hooves, head hair, body hair and rocanā (a yellow concretion from animals) are used from animals.
notes: Continues the list begun in verse 68 line 2. retas + asthi in the compound gives reto'sthi; the source writes it without avagraha (retosthi), which is acceptable inside a compound. rocanā is usually understood as gorocanā (bezoar / gallstone of cattle); the text says only rocanāḥ.

hindi: सुवर्ण, मल (किट्ट) सहित पाँच लोह (धातुएँ), सिकता (बालू), सुधा (चूना), मनःशिला और आल (हरताल), मणियाँ, लवण, गैरिक और अञ्जन —
english: Gold, the five metals with their dross, together with sand (sikatā), lime (sudhā), realgar (manaḥśilā) and orpiment (āla), gems, salt, red ochre (gairika) and collyrium (añjana) —
notes: The list continues into verse 71 line 1 ('are declared the earthly medicines'). sa-sikatāḥ is grammatically masc. pl. like samalāḥ and could qualify lohāḥ; more naturally it adds 'sands' (sikatā) as a separate item ('and sands'). The five metals are usually taken as silver, copper, lead, tin, iron (not named here). āla = haritāla (orpiment). añjana: a collyrium mineral (often stibnite/antimony). 'sasikatāḥ' is read here as sand, a separate item; it could alternatively be adjectival ('with sand') with the preceding metals.
lines_iast: suvarṇaṃ samalāḥ pañca lohāḥ sasikatāḥ sudhā
lines_deva: सुवर्णं समलाः पञ्च लोहाः ससिकताः सुधा

hindi: — (ये) भौम (पार्थिव) औषध कहे गए हैं। औद्भिद (वनस्पतिज) औषध तो चार प्रकार का है — वनस्पति, वीरुध्, वानस्पत्य और ओषधि।
english: — (these) are declared to be the earthly medicines. The plant medicines, however, are fourfold: vanaspati, vīrudh, vānaspatya and oṣadhi.
notes: Line 1 closes the list of verse 70. The four plant classes are defined in verse 72. vīrut is the nominative of vīrudh (f.).

hindi: जिनमें फल होते हैं वे वनस्पति, जिनमें पुष्प और फल भी होते हैं वे वानस्पत्य, जो फल पकने पर नष्ट हो जाती हैं वे ओषधियाँ, और जो प्रतान (फैलने वाली शाखाओं/लताओं) से युक्त हैं वे वीरुध् कही गई हैं।
english: Vanaspatis are (known) by their fruits, vānaspatyas by flowers and also fruits; oṣadhis are those whose life ends with the ripening of the fruit, and vīrudhs are known by their spreading shoots.
notes: Literally: 'vanaspati by fruits, vānaspatya by flowers and also fruits; oṣadhis ending with fruit-ripening; vīrudhs by spreading shoots are known.' The idea 'without flowers' for vanaspati is implied by the contrast, not stated; it appears in the Hindi in brackets. pratāna: tendrils / spreading branches.

words.gloss: root, bark, heartwood, exudate, stalk, expressed juice, tender leaves

hindi: मूल, त्वचा (छाल), सार, निर्यास, नाल, स्वरस, पल्लव, क्षार, क्षीर (दूध), फल, पुष्प, भस्म, तैल, काँटे —
english: Root, bark, heartwood, exudate, stalk, expressed juice, tender leaves; alkalis, latex, fruit, flower, ash, oils, thorns —
notes: The list continues into verse 74 ('... is the plant group'). Variant reading noted by the edition: -nāḍasva- for -nālasva- (nāḍa ~ nāla, 'hollow stalk'); same meaning. kṣīra here = milky latex of plants.
lines_iast: kṣārāḥ kṣīraṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ bhasma tailāni kaṇṭakāḥ
lines_deva: क्षाराः क्षीरं फलं पुष्पं भस्म तैलानि कण्टकाः

hindi: पत्र, शुंग (कोंपल), कन्द और प्ररोह — यह औद्भिद (वनस्पतिज) गण है। मूलिनी (जिनकी जड़ प्रयुक्त होती है) सोलह और फलिनी (जिनका फल प्रयुक्त होता है) बीस में एक कम (उन्नीस) मानी गई हैं।
english: Leaves, leaf-buds, tubers and sprouts — this is the group (of products) of plant origin. The mūlinīs (plants used for their roots) are known to be sixteen, and the phalinīs (plants used for their fruits) twenty less one (nineteen).
notes: ṣoḍaśaikonā = ṣoḍaśa + ekonā; ṣoḍaśa goes with mūlinyaḥ, ekonā ('less by one') with viṃśatiḥ, giving 19 phalinīs (listed in verses 81-83). śuṅga: leaf-bud / tender sheath; praroha: shoot, also aerial root.

hindi: चार महास्नेह, पाँच ही लवण, आठ मूत्र और आठ ही दूध गिनाए गए हैं।
english: The great unctuous substances (mahāsneha) are four, the salts just five; eight urines are enumerated, and likewise eight milks.

hindi: और पुनर्वसु (आत्रेय) द्वारा बताए गए छह वृक्ष शोधन के लिए हैं। जो इनका विकारों में (उचित) प्रयोग करना जानता है, वह वेद (आयुर्वेद) का ज्ञाता है।
english: And there are six trees for purification (śodhana), pointed out by Punarvasu. He who knows how to apply these in disorders is a knower of the science (veda).
notes: Punarvasu is Ātreya. etān ('these') most naturally refers to all the items listed in verses 74-76 (root- and fruit-drugs, sneha, salts, urines, milks, trees). veda-vit: literally 'knower of the Veda'; in context the science of medicine (Āyurveda).
lines_iast: ya etān vetti saṃyoktuṃ vikāreṣu sa vedavit
lines_deva: य एतान् वेत्ति संयोक्तुं विकारेषु स वेदवित्

hindi: हस्तिदन्ती, हैमवती, श्यामा, त्रिवृत्, अधोगुडा, सप्तला, श्वेता नामवाली, प्रत्यक्श्रेणी और गवाक्षी भी —
english: Hastidantī, haimavatī, śyāmā, trivṛt, adhoguḍā, saptalā, the one named śvetā, pratyakśreṇī and also gavākṣī —
notes: List of the sixteen mūlinīs, continued in verse 78 (items 1-9 here). Plant names are kept untranslated; botanical identifications are uncertain and not given in the text. śvetanāmā = 'named śvetā' (called simply śvetā in verse 79). The source writes trivṛdadhoguḍā (trivṛt + adhoguḍā); adhoguḍā is the standard form.

hindi: ज्योतिष्मती, बिम्बी, शणपुष्पी, विषाणिका, अजगन्धा, द्रवन्ती, और यहाँ सोलहवीं क्षीरिणी है।
english: Jyotiṣmatī, bimbī, śaṇapuṣpī, viṣāṇikā, ajagandhā, dravantī, and kṣīriṇī, the sixteenth here.
notes: Items 10-16 of the mūlinīs; with verse 77 the count is exactly sixteen.
lines_iast: jyotiṣmatī ca bimbī ca śaṇapuṣpī viṣāṇikā
ajagandhā dravantī ca kṣīriṇī cātra ṣoḍaśī
lines_deva: ज्योतिष्मती च बिम्बी च शणपुष्पी विषाणिका
अजगन्धा द्रवन्ती च क्षीरिणी चात्र षोडशी

hindi: शणपुष्पी, बिम्बी और हैमवती भी छर्दन (वमन) में; तथा श्वेता और ज्योतिष्मती शिरोविरेचन में प्रयोग की जानी चाहिए।
english: Śaṇapuṣpī, bimbī and also haimavatī (are used) in emesis; śvetā and jyotiṣmatī are to be used in head-purgation (śīrṣavirecana).
notes: cchardane: after ca the initial ch is doubled by sandhi (ca + chardane -> ca cchardane). yojyā is singular, applying to each plant (or to the second group). 'are used' in line 1 is supplied from yojyā.
lines_iast: śaṇapuṣpī ca bimbī ca cchardane haimavatyapi
lines_deva: शणपुष्पी च बिम्बी च च्छर्दने हैमवत्यपि

hindi: जो ग्यारह शेष बचीं, वे विरेचन में प्रयोग की जानी चाहिए। इस प्रकार नाम और कर्म के द्वारा मूलिनियाँ कही गईं; अब फलिनियों को सुनो।
english: The eleven that remain are to be used in purgation (virecana). Thus the mūlinīs have been described by name and action; now hear the phalinīs.
notes: 16 mūlinīs minus 3 (emesis) minus 2 (head-purgation) = 11 for purgation, matching the text.

words.gram: n. nom. sg. (fruit; stem usu. f.)

hindi: शंखिनी, विडंग, त्रपुष, मदन, धामार्गव, इक्ष्वाकु, जीमूत, कृतवेधन; और क्लीतक दो प्रकार का माना गया है — आनूप (जलप्राय भूमि में उत्पन्न) और स्थलज (सूखी भूमि में उत्पन्न) —
english: Śaṅkhinī, then viḍaṅga, trapuṣa and madana; dhāmārgava, then ikṣvāku, jīmūta, kṛtavedhana; and klītaka, known to be twofold — growing in marshland and growing on dry land —

text_flags.why: dvididha is not a word; dvi-vidha 'twofold' is required by sense (two kinds of klītaka) and parallels tri-vidha / catur-vidha in this chunk. Metre is unaffected.

notes: List of the nineteen phalinīs (items 1-10 here: śaṅkhinī, viḍaṅga, trapuṣa, madana, dhāmārgava, ikṣvāku, jīmūta, kṛtavedhana, and the two klītakas); it continues in verses 82-83. This unit has three half-lines in the source (the verse division differs from a strict two-line grouping); the line 'dhāmārgavamathekṣvāku jīmūtaṃ kṛtavedhanam' occurs again as verse 83 line 2, where it begins the statement of uses — that repetition appears to be genuine, since both occurrences are needed: in 81 the four fruits are members of the list (giving 19 with 82 and 83 line 1); in 83 they begin the list of uses (8 for emesis/āsthāpana + 1 nasal = 9, leaving 10 for purgation, as verse 85 states). klītaka is commonly identified with liquorice (madhuyaṣṭī); the text gives no identification. viḍaṅgāni and madanāni are plural (the fruits).
lines_iast: ānūpaṃ sthalajaṃ caiva klītakaṃ dvididhaṃ smṛtam
lines_deva: आनूपं स्थलजं चैव क्लीतकं द्विदिधं स्मृतम्

hindi: प्रकीर्या, उदकीर्या, प्रत्यक्पुष्पा, अभया, अन्तःकोटरपुष्पी, और हस्तिपर्णी का शरद् ऋतु में होने वाला (फल) —
english: Prakīryā and udakīryā, pratyakpuṣpā, likewise abhayā, antaḥkoṭarapuṣpī, and the autumnal (fruit) of hastiparṇī —
notes: Phalinīs 11-16. codakīryā = ca + udakīryā. hastiparṇyāḥ is genitive: 'the autumnal (fruit) of hastiparṇī'; phalam is understood with śāradam (neuter). abhayā is usually identified as harītakī.
lines_deva: प्रकीर्या चोदकीर्या च प्रत्यक्पुष्पा तथा ऽभया

hindi: कम्पिल्लक और आरग्वध का फल, तथा कुटज का जो फल है — (ये फलिनियाँ हैं)। धामार्गव, इक्ष्वाकु, जीमूत, कृतवेधन —
english: The fruit of kampillaka and of āragvadha, and that of kuṭaja (complete the phalinīs). Dhāmārgava, ikṣvāku, jīmūta, kṛtavedhana —
notes: Line 1 gives phalinīs 17-19 (kampillaka, āragvadha, kuṭaja), completing the nineteen. Line 2 repeats verse 81 line 2 verbatim; it is not a new list item but the start of a new sentence continued in verse 84 ('... these are to be used in emesis and āsthāpana'). This reading is supported by verse 85: 8 emetics (these four + madana, kuṭaja, trapuṣa, hastiparṇinī) + pratyakpuṣpā = 9, leaving the stated ten of nineteen for purgation. If instead the repetition were a copying error, the count in verse 85 would fail, so it is not flagged. yat ... kuṭajasya ca: literally 'and the (fruit) which is of kuṭaja'.

hindi: — मदन, कुटज, त्रपुष और हस्तिपर्णिनी — इन (आठों) का प्रयोग वमन में और आस्थापन (निरूह बस्ति) में भी करना चाहिए।
english: — madana, kuṭaja, trapuṣa and hastiparṇinī: these are to be used in emesis (vamana) and also in āsthāpana (decoction enemas).
notes: Continues the sentence begun in verse 83 line 2; etāni covers all eight fruits named there and here. hastiparṇinī = hastiparṇī of verse 82. āsthāpana: the (non-oily) decoction enema.

hindi: और नासिका द्वारा (दोषों के) निष्कासन में प्रत्यक्पुष्पा का विधान किया गया है। जो दस शेष बचे हैं, वे विरेचन में (प्रयोज्य) कहे गए हैं।
english: And pratyakpuṣpā is prescribed for evacuation through the nose. The ten that remain are stated for purgation (virecana).
notes: nastaḥ pracchardana: literally 'expulsion through the nose', i.e. a nasal evacuative (errhine) therapy, comparable to śīrṣavirecana in verse 79; one could also read nastaḥ-pracchardana as a compound. Count: 19 - 8 - 1 = 10, as stated.

hindi: उन्नीस फल नाम और कर्म के द्वारा कहे गए। सर्पि (घी), तैल, वसा और मज्जा — स्नेह चार प्रकार का बताया गया है।
english: The nineteen fruits have been stated by name and action. Ghee, oil, fat and marrow: sneha (unctuous substance) is indicated to be fourfold.
notes: sarpistailaṃ could also be taken as a dvandva compound sarpis-tailam; the meaning is the same. diṣṭa ('indicated, prescribed') from √diś. These four are the mahāsnehas of verse 75.

hindi: पान, अभ्यंग, बस्ति और नस्य के लिए योग (उचित प्रयोग) के अनुसार प्रयुक्त ये स्नेह स्नेहन करने वाले, जीवन देने वाले, वर्ण को उत्तम करने वाले तथा बल और उपचय (शरीर की पुष्टि) को बढ़ाने वाले हैं।
english: Used, by proper application, for drinking, inunction, enema and nasal administration, these fats are oleating, vitalizing, good for the complexion, and increase strength and bodily growth.
notes: Continues the description of the four snehas (fats) from the preceding verses; the sentence runs on into verse 88a. 'yogataḥ' can also mean 'in combination (with other drugs)'.

hindi: ये स्नेह वात, पित्त और कफ को दूर करने वाले बताए गए हैं। सौवर्चल, सैन्धव, विड और औद्भिद भी (लवण हैं)।
english: And these fats are prescribed as removers of Vāta, Pitta and Kapha. Sauvarcala, saindhava (rock salt), viḍa and audbhida as well —
notes: Line 2 begins the list of salts, which continues in verse 89 (with sāmudra making five).

hindi: सामुद्र लवण के साथ ये पाँच लवण हैं; ये स्निग्ध, उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण और अत्यन्त दीपनीय (अग्नि को प्रदीप्त करने वाले) हैं।
english: These, together with sea salt, are the five salts; they are unctuous, hot, sharp and the most stimulating to digestion (dīpanīya).

text_flags.why: 'snighd-' is not a Sanskrit form; the word is snigdha 'unctuous' (cf. snigdhaṃ in verses 100, 107). Transposition of g/gh-d/dh in data entry.

words.gloss: in downward and upward evacuation (purgation, emesis)

hindi: (ये लवण) आलेप के लिए, स्नेहन और स्वेदन की विधि में, तथा अधोभाग और ऊर्ध्वभाग (विरेचन और वमन) के शोधनों में, निरूह बस्तियों में और अनुवासन में प्रयुक्त होते हैं।
english: They are used for pastes (ālepana), likewise in oleation and sudation procedures, in evacuations of the lower and upper parts (purgation and emesis), in decoction enemas (nirūha) and in oil enema (anuvāsana);
notes: adhobhāga / ūrdhvabhāga literally 'lower part / upper part'; here, as usual in Caraka, the evacuative therapies through those routes (virecana, vamana). The list continues in verses 91-92.

hindi: अभ्यंग में, भोजन के लिए, सिर के विरेचन (शिरोविरेचन) में, शस्त्रकर्म में, वर्ति बनाने के लिए, तथा अञ्जन और उत्सादन में भी (लवण प्रयुक्त होते हैं)।
english: in inunction, in food, in evacuation of the head, in surgical procedures, for making suppositories (varti), and in collyrium (añjana) and unction (utsādana);

text_flags.why: 'cirecane' is not a word; śirasaś ca virecane 'and in evacuation of the head' (śirovirecana) is required by sense, and virecane occurs elsewhere in this chunk (95, 112, 115). c/v confusion in data entry.

notes: varti: a medicated wick or suppository (rectal, vaginal, or for the eye).

hindi: अजीर्ण और आनाह में, वात रोग में, गुल्म, शूल तथा उदर रोग में (भी लवण प्रयुक्त होते हैं)। लवणों का वर्णन हो गया; अब आगे मुझसे आठ मूत्रों को जानो।
english: in indigestion and distension (ānāha), in Vāta disorders, in gulma (abdominal lump), colic, and also in udara (abdominal enlargement). The salts have been described; hereafter learn from me the eight urines.
notes: Tool flag: a stray '&' in the source was removed; the word division as given (ajīrṇānāhayor vāte) is sound and the line scans as 16 syllables. 'vāte' may be read as 'in Vāta (disorders)'.
src_flags: source has stray "&" before a word; removed, check word division

hindi: आत्रेय के उपदेश में जो सब मुख्य (मूत्र) बताए गए हैं, (वे ये हैं): भेड़ का मूत्र, बकरी का मूत्र, गोमूत्र और जो भैंस का (मूत्र) है,
english: All those that are taught as the principal ones in Ātreya's teaching: sheep's urine, goat's urine, cow's urine, and that of the buffalo,
notes: The list of eight runs into verse 94a.

hindi: हाथी का मूत्र, तथा ऊँट, घोड़े और गधे का (मूत्र)। (मूत्र सामान्यतः) उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, अरूक्ष (रूखा नहीं), कटु और लवण रस से युक्त होता है।
english: elephant's urine, and that of the camel, the horse and the donkey. Urine is hot, sharp, not dry, pungent, and has a salty taste.
notes: The avagraha in atho 'rūkṣaṃ gives arūkṣa 'not dry'; read without it (atho rūkṣaṃ) the sense would be the opposite, 'and dry'. The metre is the same either way. The given text is followed here. Line 2 states properties common to all urines (singular 'mūtram' understood).

hindi: मूत्र उत्सादन में उपयुक्त है, आलेपों में उपयुक्त है; मूत्र आस्थापन (बस्ति) में उपयुक्त है और विरेचन में भी उपयुक्त है।
english: Urine is suitable for unction (utsādana) and suitable for pastes; urine is suitable for decoction enema (āsthāpana) and also suitable for purgation;
notes: yukta 'joined, applied' is rendered 'suitable/used'.

words.gloss: in patients of gulma, kuṣṭha, kilāsa

hindi: स्वेदन में भी, आनाह में और अगद (विषनाशक योगों) में भी वह उपयुक्त है; तथा उदर रोगों, अर्श में और गुल्म, कुष्ठ तथा किलास के रोगियों में (भी उपयुक्त है)।
english: it is also suitable in sudation, in distension (ānāha) and in antidotes (agada); and in abdominal diseases (udara), in piles, and for patients with gulma, kuṣṭha (skin disease) and kilāsa (white patches of skin);
notes: gulmin, kuṣṭhin, kilāsin = persons suffering from these diseases.

hindi: वह उपनाह (पुल्टिस) में और उसी प्रकार परिषेक में भी उपयुक्त है; और उसे दीपनीय, विषनाशक और कृमिनाशक बताया जाता है।
english: it is suitable in poultices (upanāha) and likewise in affusion (pariṣeka); and it is declared to be stimulating to digestion, destructive of poison and destructive of worms.

words.gloss: would move in its proper direction

hindi: और पाण्डु रोग से पीड़ित लोगों के लिए इसे उत्तम सुखकारक (उपाय) कहा जाता है। पीने पर यह श्लेष्मा (कफ) का शमन करता है और मारुत (वात) का अनुलोमन करता है,
english: And it is said to be the best relief for those afflicted with pāṇḍu-roga (anaemia). Drunk, it pacifies Kapha (śleṣman) and makes Vāta (māruta) move in its proper downward direction,

text_flags.why: upa-sṛṣṭa 'afflicted' has retroflex ṣṭ; 'sṛṣt' (dental t after ṣ) is a data-entry slip.

notes: śarma literally 'shelter, comfort'. anulomayet: causes it to move along its natural course (anuloma).

hindi: और पित्त को अधोभाग (नीचे के मार्ग) की ओर खींचता है। इस प्रकार इस (मूत्र) के गुणों का संग्रह मैंने सामान्य रूप से कहा है; अब (प्रत्येक का) अलग-अलग वर्णन किया जाएगा।
english: and draws Pitta downward. Thus the summary of its properties has been stated by me in general terms; now it will be set out for each one separately.
notes: 'asmin' may refer to urine (mūtra) or to 'this (section)'. pravakṣyate is formally a future middle with passive sense ('will be told').

hindi: भेड़ का मूत्र कुछ तिक्त, स्निग्ध और पित्त का अविरोधी (पित्त के प्रतिकूल नहीं) होता है। बकरी का मूत्र कषाय-मधुर, पथ्य है और दोषों का नाश करता है।
english: Sheep's urine is slightly bitter, unctuous and not antagonistic to Pitta. Goat's urine is astringent and sweet, wholesome, and destroys the doṣas.
notes: sa-tikta: literally 'with bitterness', i.e. having a secondary bitter taste.
lines_iast: avimūtraṃ satiktaṃ syāt snigdhaṃ pittāvirodhi ca
lines_deva: अविमूत्रं सतिक्तं स्यात् स्निग्धं पित्ताविरोधि च

hindi: गाय का मूत्र थोड़ा मधुर, दोषनाशक, कृमि और कुष्ठ को दूर करने वाला है; पीने पर यह खुजली का शमन करता है और दोषज उदर रोग में भली-भाँति हितकर है।
english: Cow's urine is slightly sweet, destroys the doṣas, and removes worms and kuṣṭha (skin disease); drunk, it relieves itching and is properly beneficial in udara (abdominal disease) caused by the doṣas.
notes: 'kiṃcit' may go with 'samadhuram' (slightly sweet, as taken here) or with 'doṣaghnam' (slightly doṣa-destroying); word order favours the latter, sense and parallels (satiktam = slightly bitter) the former. 'samyak' may qualify 'pītam' (when drunk properly) or 'hitam' (properly beneficial).
lines_iast: kaṇḍūṃ ca śamayet pītaṃ samyagdoṣodare hitam
lines_deva: कण्डूं च शमयेत् पीतं सम्यग्दोषोदरे हितम्

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first)

words.gloss: for those with worms and kuṣṭha

hindi: भैंस का मूत्र अर्श, शोथ और उदर रोग का नाशक, क्षारयुक्त और सर (मल को सरकाने वाला) है। हाथी का मूत्र लवण रस वाला है और कृमि तथा कुष्ठ के रोगियों के लिए हितकर है,
english: Buffalo's urine destroys piles, swelling (śopha) and udara, is alkaline and laxative. Elephant's urine is salty and beneficial for those suffering from worms and kuṣṭha,
notes: krimikuṣṭhinām: 'those having worms and kuṣṭha' (krimin + kuṣṭhin, or krimi-kuṣṭha + -in). The description of elephant's urine continues in 103a.
lines_iast: hāstikaṃ lavaṇaṃ mūtraṃ hitaṃ tu krimikuṣṭhinām
lines_deva: हास्तिकं लवणं मूत्रं हितं तु क्रिमिकुष्ठिनाम्

words.gloss: for retention of faeces and urine, poison, Kapha diseases, piles

hindi: (और हाथी का मूत्र) बँधे हुए मल-मूत्र, विष, श्लेष्मज रोगों और अर्श में प्रशस्त है। ऊँट का मूत्र कुछ तिक्त, श्वास और कास का नाशक तथा अर्श का नाशक कहा जाता है।
english: and (elephant's urine) is commended for retention of faeces and urine, poison, diseases of Kapha (śleṣman) and piles. Camel's urine is said to be slightly bitter and to destroy dyspnoea (śvāsa), cough (kāsa) and piles.
notes: 103a is taken as continuing the elephant's urine of 102b; it could grammatically be read as the start of the camel's description, but 103b has its own subject (auṣṭram) and the sense joins 103a to the preceding. The genitive plural compound may be read as 'for (patients of) ...'. śleṣmāmaya: 'disease of Kapha' (or 'Kapha and āma'; less likely).

hindi: घोड़ों का (मूत्र) तिक्त-कटु और कुष्ठ, व्रण तथा विष को दूर करने वाला है। गधे का मूत्र अपस्मार, उन्माद और ग्रह (बाधा) का नाश करने वाला है।
english: That of horses is bitter and pungent and removes kuṣṭha, wounds (vraṇa) and poison. Donkey's urine destroys epilepsy (apasmāra), insanity (unmāda) and possession (graha).
notes: graha: seizure by malevolent beings ('possession'); commentators also explain it as a class of disorders. vājinām: 'mūtram' understood.

hindi: इस प्रकार यहाँ मूत्रों का वर्णन उनकी सामर्थ्य और प्रयोग के अनुसार किया गया। अब दूधों का वर्णन किया जाएगा, और उनका कर्म तथा उनके जो गुण हैं (उनका भी)।
english: Thus the urines have been described here according to their potency and application. Hereafter the milks will be described, with their action and the qualities they have.
notes: yathāsāmarthyayogataḥ may also be read 'as far as their potency allows them to be used' or 'according to (their) power and combination'.
lines_iast: ataḥ kṣīrāṇi vakṣyante karma caiṣāṃ guṇāśca ye
lines_deva: अतः क्षीराणि वक्ष्यन्ते कर्म चैषां गुणाश्च ये

hindi: भेड़ का दूध, बकरी का दूध, गाय का दूध और जो भैंस का (दूध) है, तथा ऊँटनियों का, हथिनियों का, घोड़ी का और उसी प्रकार स्त्री का (दूध)।
english: Sheep's milk, goat's milk, cow's milk and that of the buffalo; then that of she-camels, of she-elephants, of the mare, and likewise of woman.
notes: The eight milks, parallel to the eight urines of verse 93-94.

hindi: दूध प्रायः मधुर, स्निग्ध, शीत और स्तन्य (स्तनों में दूध बढ़ाने वाला) माना गया है; वह प्रीणन (तृप्ति देने वाला), बृंहण (पुष्टिकारक), वृष्य, मेध्य (बुद्धिवर्धक), बल्य और मन को बल देने वाला है।
english: Milk is generally considered sweet, unctuous, cold and promoting breast-milk; it is nourishing, bulk-building (bṛṃhaṇa), aphrodisiac, good for the intellect, strengthening and invigorating to the mind,
notes: stanya here is taken as 'galactagogue' (promoting lactation); it could also be read as 'like breast-milk' or simply 'breast milk', but in a list of properties the galactagogue sense fits. manaskara: literally 'making mind'.
lines_iast: prāyaśo madhuraṃ snigdhaṃ śītaṃ stanyaṃ payo matam
prīṇanaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vṛṣyaṃ medhyaṃ balyaṃ manaskaram
lines_deva: प्रायशो मधुरं स्निग्धं शीतं स्तन्यं पयो मतम्
प्रीणनं बृंहणं वृष्यं मेध्यं बल्यं मनस्करम्

hindi: जीवनीय, श्रम को हरने वाला, श्वास और कास का नाश करने वाला है; यह रक्तपित्त का नाश करता है और टूटे या आहत (अंग) को जोड़ने वाला है।
english: vitalizing, removing fatigue, destroying dyspnoea and cough; it destroys śoṇitapitta (bleeding disorder) and heals (unites) what is injured,
notes: śoṇitapitta = raktapitta (haemorrhagic disorder). sandhānaṃ vihatasya: 'a uniter of the injured (or fractured)'.
lines_iast: hanti śoṇitapittaṃ ca sandhānaṃ vihatasya ca
lines_deva: हन्ति शोणितपित्तं च सन्धानं विहतस्य च

hindi: यह सभी प्राणियों के लिए सात्म्य (अनुकूल) है, शमन और शोधन दोनों करने वाला है, प्यास को मिटाने वाला और दीपनीय है, तथा क्षीण और क्षत (रोगियों) में श्रेष्ठ है।
english: congenial (sātmya) to all living beings, both pacifying and purifying, removing thirst and stimulating digestion, and the best (remedy) for the wasted and the injured (kṣīṇa-kṣata);

text_flags.why: possible typo: the usual compound is prāṇa-bhṛt 'bearer of breath, living being'; long ā before bhṛt is irregular. Metre allows either (16 syllables, 5th syllable light in both).

notes: śamana / śodhana: the two kinds of therapy (palliative and evacuative). kṣīṇa-kṣata may also be read as one condition, 'wasting due to (chest) injury' (urahkṣata).
lines_iast: tṛṣṇāghnaṃ dīpanīyaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ kṣīṇakṣateṣu ca
lines_deva: तृष्णाघ्नं दीपनीयं च श्रेष्ठं क्षीणक्षतेषु च

hindi: पाण्डु रोग, अम्लपित्त, शोष, गुल्म तथा उदर रोग में, अतिसार, ज्वर, दाह में और विशेष रूप से शोथ (सूजन) में (दूध हितकर है)।
english: (it is beneficial) in pāṇḍu-roga (anaemia), amlapitta (acid dyspepsia), śoṣa (wasting), gulma and udara, in diarrhoea, fever, burning sensation, and especially in swelling (śvayathu);
notes: The locatives depend on 'pathyam' in 111b.
lines_iast: atīsāre jvare dāhe śvayathau ca viśeṣataḥ
lines_deva: पाण्डुरोगे ऽम्लपित्ते च शोषे गुल्मे तथोदरे
अतीसारे ज्वरे दाहे श्वयथौ च विशेषतः

words.gloss: in disorders of the female genital tract and semen

hindi: योनि और शुक्र के दोषों में, मूत्र के अल्प होने पर, और मल के गाँठदार (कठिन) होने पर (दूध) वात-पित्त के विकारों से पीड़ितों के लिए पथ्य है।
english: in disorders of the female genital tract (yoni) and of semen, when urine is scanty, and when the faeces are knotted (hard), it is wholesome for those suffering from disorders of Vāta and Pitta.
notes: mūtreṣv apracureṣu and purīṣe grathite are locative absolutes ('when urine is scanty', 'when faeces are hard').

words.gloss: in nasal therapy, pastes and immersion baths

hindi: नस्य, आलेप, अवगाह (टब-स्नान), वमन, आस्थापन, विरेचन और स्नेहन में — सर्वत्र दूध का प्रयोग होता है।
english: In nasal therapy, pastes, immersion baths (avagāha), emesis, decoction enema, purgation and oleation — milk is used everywhere.
lines_iast: virecane snehane ca payaḥ sarvatra yujyate
lines_deva: विरेचने स्नेहने च पयः सर्वत्र युज्यते

hindi: दूधों के गुणों को क्रम से, प्रत्येक के अलग-अलग, मैं आगे 'अन्नपान' आदि वाले अध्याय में फिर से पूर्ण रूप से कहूँगा।
english: The qualities of the milks, in due order and of each one separately, I shall describe further and in full in the chapter (concerned with) food, drink and the rest (annapāna-ādi).
notes: annapānādike 'dhyāye: 'in the chapter beginning with / concerning food and drink'; refers to the later chapter on food and drink (Annapānavidhi, Sū. 27), but the identification is not stated in the text.

words.gloss: from the fruit- and root-yielding plants
words.gram: m./n. inst. pl. of phalamūlin (dvandva phala-mūla + poss. -in)

hindi: अब तीन अन्य वृक्ष हैं जो फलिनी और मूलिनी (औषधियों) से भिन्न हैं — स्नुही, अर्क और अश्मन्तक; उनका अलग-अलग कर्म यह है:
english: Now there are three other plants, distinct from the fruit-yielding and root-yielding ones: snuhī, arka and aśmantaka. Their action, each separately, is as follows:
notes: phalamūlibhiḥ is taken as the phalinī (fruit-yielding) and mūlinī (root-yielding) plants listed earlier in the chapter; pṛthak governs the instrumental ('apart from'). Some take it as 'distinct in (their) fruits and roots'. snuhī = a Euphorbia, arka = Calotropis, aśmantaka: identification uncertain.

hindi: अश्मन्तक को वमन में, स्नुही के दूध (क्षीर) को विरेचन में (उपयोगी) जानना चाहिए; अर्क का दूध वमन और विरेचन (दोनों) में (उपयोगी) जानना चाहिए।
english: One should know aśmantaka as used for emesis and the latex of snuhī for purgation; the latex of arka is to be known as used for emesis as well as purgation.
notes: kṣīra here is the milky latex of the plant. 'savirecane' qualifies vamane: 'in emesis together with purgation'.

hindi: इन तीन अन्य वृक्षों को (भी) बताया गया है, जिनकी छालें हितकर हैं — पूतीक, कृष्णगन्धा और उसी प्रकार तिल्वक वृक्ष।
english: They speak of these three other trees whose barks are beneficial: Pūtīka, Kṛṣṇagandhā, and likewise the tree Tilvaka.
notes: "aparān" (other) contrasts these three bark-trees with the three latex-trees listed just before. "tathā taruḥ" is literally "and likewise the tree", i.e. Tilvaka, which is a tree. Identifications of the plants (e.g. Kṛṣṇagandhā as śigru) belong to the commentaries, not this text.
lines_iast: pūtīkaḥ kṛṣṇagandhā ca tilvakaśca tathā taruḥ
lines_deva: पूतीकः कृष्णगन्धा च तिल्वकश्च तथा तरुः

words.gram: fut. pass. part. pra-√yuj, m. nom. sg.

hindi: विरेचन में पूतीक और उसी प्रकार तिल्वक का प्रयोग करना चाहिए; कृष्णगन्धा परीसर्प, शोथ और अर्श में (प्रयोग के योग्य) बताई गई है।
english: Pūtīka and likewise Tilvaka are to be used in purgation; Kṛṣṇagandhā is prescribed for parīsarpa (a spreading skin disease), swellings and piles.

text_flags.why: possible: loc. pl. of arśas is arśaḥsu (or arśassu); after visarga preceded by a the s is not retroflexed, so ṣ looks like a typo or orthographic slip (the Devanagari has the same ष).

notes: "prayoktavyaḥ" is singular though it governs two subjects (Pūtīka and Tilvaka); it agrees with the nearer one or each separately. "ucyate" is literally "is said", i.e. said to be indicated. The list of conditions for Kṛṣṇagandhā continues into the next verse.

words.gram: saṃkhyā-pūrva karmadhāraya (or ṣaṭ + vṛkṣān), m. acc. pl.

hindi: (कृष्णगन्धा) दद्रु, विद्रधि, गण्ड, कुष्ठ और अलजी में भी (प्रयुक्त होती है)। विचक्षण (वैद्य) इन छह वृक्षों को शोधन (करने वाले) भी जाने।
english: (Kṛṣṇagandhā is also used) in ringworm, abscess, gaṇḍa (glandular swellings), kuṣṭha (skin diseases) and alajī (pustular eruptions). The discerning (physician) should also know these six trees as purifying (śodhana).
notes: The first line continues the uses of Kṛṣṇagandhā from v. 117 (loc. pl. parallel to parīsarpe etc.). "ṣaḍvṛkṣān" can be read as a dvigu compound or as two words ṣaṭ vṛkṣān; the sense is the same. "ñch" is sandhi of -n + ś-. gaṇḍa may mean goitre/glandular swelling or boil.

words.gloss: whose milk and bark are indicated

hindi: इस प्रकार फलिनी और मूलिनी (औषधियाँ), स्नेह, लवण, मूत्र, दूध और वे छह वृक्ष, जिनका दूध (क्षीर) और छाल (उपयोगी) बताए गए हैं — (इन सबका) वर्णन किया गया।
english: Thus have been stated the fruit-plants and root-plants, the fats, the salts, urine, the milks, and the six trees whose milk (latex) and bark have been indicated.
notes: Summary of the preceding section. "diṣṭapayastvacaḥ" is taken as a bahuvrīhi: diṣṭa (indicated) + payas (milk, i.e. latex) + tvac (bark): "whose milk and bark are indicated" (three trees for latex, three for bark). The compound reading fits the metre (16 syllables). "phalamūlinyaḥ" = phalinyaḥ and mūlinyaḥ (cf. v. 138 mūlinyaś ca phalinyaś ca).
lines_iast: mūtraṃ kṣīrāṇi vṛkṣāśca ṣaḍ ye diṣṭapayastvacaḥ
lines_deva: मूत्रं क्षीराणि वृक्षाश्च षड् ये दिष्टपयस्त्वचः

hindi: वन में बकरी चराने वाले, भेड़ चराने वाले, ग्वाले और अन्य जो वनवासी हैं, वे औषधियों को नाम और रूप से जानते ही हैं।
english: Goatherds in the forest, as well as shepherds, cowherds and other forest-dwellers, do indeed know the medicinal plants by name and form.
notes: "vane" (in the forest) may go with ajapāḥ only or with the whole list. The point is completed in the next two verses: such knowledge alone is not enough.

hindi: केवल नाम के ज्ञान से, अथवा रूप के ज्ञान से भी, कोई औषधियों की परम प्राप्ति (पूर्ण ज्ञान) को नहीं जान सकता।
english: No one can know the highest attainment (i.e. the full understanding) of medicinal plants merely by knowing their names, or again by knowing their form.
notes: "parāṃ prāptim" is literally "the highest attainment"; it is understood as full, practical understanding of the plants, as v. 122 shows (knowledge of their use, yoga).

hindi: किन्तु जो उनके प्रयोग (योग) को जानता है, वह रूप न जानते हुए भी उनका तत्त्वज्ञ कहा जाता है; फिर उस वैद्य का तो कहना ही क्या जो औषधियों को सब प्रकार से जानता हो।
english: But one who knows their application, even without knowing their form, is called a knower of their true nature; how much more, then, the physician who knows the plants in every respect.
notes: "kiṃ punaḥ" = "what to say of / how much more". "tāsām" (f.) refers to the oṣadhīs; it can be construed with both yogavit and tattvavit.

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, caus. pp. upa-√pad, m. acc. sg.
fut. pass. part. √jñā, m. nom. sg.

hindi: किन्तु जो प्रत्येक व्यक्ति को देखकर (परखकर) इन (औषधियों) के देश और काल के अनुसार निर्धारित प्रयोग को जानता है, उसे श्रेष्ठ वैद्य समझना चाहिए।
english: But he who, examining each individual person, knows the application of these (plants) as adapted to place and time, should be known as the best of physicians.
notes: "puruṣaṃ puruṣam" is the distributive repetition: "each person individually". "upapāditam" (caus. pp. of upa-√pad) = "arranged, worked out, made suitable" with reference to place and time.
lines_iast: puruṣaṃ puruṣaṃ vīkṣya sa jñeyo bhiṣaguttamaḥ
lines_deva: पुरुषं पुरुषं वीक्ष्य स ज्ञेयो भिषगुत्तमः

hindi: जैसे विष, जैसे शस्त्र, जैसे अग्नि और जैसे वज्र (होते हैं), वैसे ही अज्ञात औषध (घातक) है; और भली-भाँति ज्ञात (औषध) अमृत के समान है।
english: Like poison, like a weapon, like fire, like a thunderbolt is a medicine that is not (properly) known; when well known, it is like nectar (amṛta).
notes: The source writes "yathā 'gnir" with an avagraha after long ā (standard sandhi would give yathāgnir); the restored words are yathā + agniḥ. "vijñātam amṛtaṃ yathā": supply "auṣadham" (a known medicine is like amṛta).
lines_deva: यथा विषं यथा शस्त्रं यथा ऽग्निरशनिर्यथा

hindi: क्योंकि जो औषध नाम, रूप और गुण — इन तीनों से न जाना गया हो, अथवा जाना हुआ होकर भी गलत ढंग से प्रयुक्त हो, वह अनर्थ (हानि) का कारण बनता है।
english: For a medicine not known by these three, name, form and qualities, or one that, though known, is wrongly applied, leads to harm.
notes: "guṇa" here means the properties of the drug (quality, guṇa).

hindi: उचित प्रयोग (योग) से तीक्ष्ण विष भी उत्तम औषध बन सकता है; और औषध भी गलत ढंग से प्रयुक्त होने पर तीक्ष्ण विष बन जाता है।
english: Through proper application even a potent poison may become an excellent medicine; and a medicine, too, when wrongly applied, becomes a potent poison.
notes: "tīkṣṇam" can be read with viṣam in both lines ("sharp/potent poison"), which is the natural parallel; in line 1 it could also qualify bheṣajam ("a potent, excellent medicine").
lines_iast: bheṣajaṃ cāpi duryuktaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ saṃpadyate viṣam
lines_deva: भेषजं चापि दुर्युक्तं तीक्ष्णं संपद्यते विषम्

words.gram: fut. pass. part. ā-√dā, n. nom. sg.

hindi: इसलिए जीवन और आरोग्य की इच्छा रखने वाले बुद्धिमान व्यक्ति को युक्ति से रहित वैद्य द्वारा दी गई कोई भी औषध ग्रहण नहीं करनी चाहिए।
english: Therefore a wise person who desires life and health should not accept any medicine at all administered by a physician who is devoid of yukti (rational planning of treatment).
notes: "yuktibāhya" = "outside of yukti", i.e. one who does not apply reasoned planning. "yuktam" = "prescribed, administered".

hindi: सिर पर गिरा हुआ इन्द्र का वज्र (मनुष्य को) कुछ शेष (जीवित) छोड़ भी दे, किन्तु अज्ञानी द्वारा बताई गई औषध रोगी को शेष (जीवित) नहीं छोड़ती।
english: Indra's thunderbolt, falling on one's head, might yet leave something remaining (leave one alive); but a medicine prescribed by an ignorant person would not leave the patient with anything remaining.
notes: "saśeṣam" (literally "with a remainder") in line 1 has an implied object (the person struck). vāsava = Indra. "ajñamata" = "approved/advised by an ignorant person".

words.gram: pres. part. śrad-√dhā, m. dat. sg.

hindi: जो अपने को बुद्धिमान मानने वाला (व्यक्ति) औषध को बिना जाने दुःखी, शय्या पर पड़े, श्रद्धा रखने वाले रोगी को (औषध) देता है —
english: He who, thinking himself wise, gives a medicine without knowing it to a sick person who is suffering, bedridden and trusting (in him) —
notes: Relative clause (yaḥ) completed by v. 130 (tasya, "of him"). The two verses form one sentence; read together. "avijñāya" is a negated absolutive (formally irregular, but usual in this text).

hindi: (ऐसे) धर्म को त्याग देने वाले, पापी, मृत्यु-रूप, दुर्बुद्धि (वैद्य) से बात करने मात्र से भी मनुष्य नरक में गिरने वाला हो जाता है।
english: Even by conversing with such a one, who has abandoned dharma, is sinful, is death incarnate and evil-minded, a man would fall into hell.
notes: Continues v. 129: the genitives describe the ignorant giver of medicine (yaḥ ... prayacchati), resumed by "tasya". "tasya saṃbhāṣaṇāt" = "from conversation with him".

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, n. nom. sg. (āśīviṣa: bahuvrīhi 'poison-fanged', snake)
tat-puruṣa, pp. sam-√tap, m. nom. pl.

hindi: साँप का विष पी लेना, अथवा खौलता हुआ (पिघला) ताँबा पी लेना, अथवा अत्यधिक अग्नि में तपाए हुए लोहे के गोले निगल लेना भी अच्छा है —
english: Better to drink a snake's venom or even boiling (molten) copper, or to swallow iron balls heated in an intense fire —
notes: "varam ... na tu" (v. 132) = "better X ... but not Y": the two verses form one sentence. "pītam" goes with āśīviṣaviṣam and tāmram; "bhakṣitāḥ" with ayoguḍāḥ. The source writes "vā 'pi" with avagraha after ā (standard sandhi would give vāpi). "kvathita" literally "boiled".

words.gloss: from one who has sought refuge

hindi: किन्तु विद्वानों का वेश धारण करने वाले (अज्ञानी) के द्वारा, शरण में आए हुए रोग-पीड़ित व्यक्ति से अन्न, पान या धन लेना (अच्छा) नहीं है।
english: But not (is it better) for one who wears the garb of the learned to have taken food, drink or money from a disease-afflicted person who has come to him for refuge.

text_flags.why: possible: 'garb, dress' is normally veṣa; veśa (dwelling) and veṣa are often confused in manuscripts and editions, so this may be an orthographic variant rather than a real error.

notes: Completes v. 131 (varam ... na tu). "natu" is written as one token in the source; it is na + tu. "śrutavatāṃ veśaṃ bibhratā" = a pretender who only looks like a learned physician. "gṛhītam" is the impersonal predicate parallel to "pītam" in v. 131.
lines_iast: gṛhītamannaṃ pānaṃ vā vittaṃ vā rogapīḍitāt
lines_deva: गृहीतमन्नं पानं वा वित्तं वा रोगपीडितात्

hindi: इसलिए वैद्य बनने की इच्छा रखने वाला बुद्धिमान व्यक्ति अपने गुणों की सम्पत्ति (को प्राप्त करने) में परम प्रयत्न करे, जिससे वह मनुष्यों का प्राणदाता हो सके।
english: Therefore an intelligent person who wishes to become a physician should make the utmost effort towards the perfection of his own qualities, so that he may be a giver of life to people.
notes: "bhiṣag bubhūṣuḥ" is taken as "wishing to be a physician" (bhiṣak predicative with the desiderative of √bhū). An alternative reading: "a physician desiring to prosper" (bubhūṣu can mean wishing for well-being). "sampad" = "abundance, perfection, accomplishment". Line 1, odd pāda: syllables 5-7 are G L L, a regular bha-vipulā; the metre is sound.

hindi: वही औषध (चिकित्सा) उचित है जो आरोग्य प्रदान करने में समर्थ हो; और वही वैद्यों में श्रेष्ठ है जो (रोगियों को) रोगों से मुक्त कर दे।
english: That alone is proper medicine which conduces to health; and he alone is the best of physicians who frees (people) from diseases.
notes: "bhaiṣajya" can mean both a medicine and treatment in general. The object of pramocayet (the patient) is implied.
lines_iast: sa caiva bhiṣajāṃ śreṣṭho rogebhyo yaḥ pramocayet
lines_deva: स चैव भिषजां श्रेष्ठो रोगेभ्यो यः प्रमोचयेत्

hindi: सिद्धि (सफलता) सभी कर्मों के सम्यक् प्रयोग को प्रकट करती है; और सिद्धि सभी गुणों से युक्त श्रेष्ठ वैद्य को प्रकट करती है।
english: Success proclaims the correct application of all procedures; and success proclaims the best physician, endowed with all the qualities.
notes: "karma" here = therapeutic procedures/actions. "bhiṣaktama" is the superlative of bhiṣaj ("most physician-like", the best physician). "ca" in line 2 links the two statements.

lead_in_english: Here are the verses (summarising the chapter).

words.gloss: of the received teaching / of the coming

hindi: आयुर्वेद का आगमन, (उसका) हेतु, आगम (प्राप्त ज्ञान) का प्रवर्तन, (तन्त्रों की) रचना का अनुमोदन, आयुर्वेद का निर्णय (परिभाषा) —
english: The coming of Āyurveda (the science of life), its cause, the propagation of the received teaching, the approval of the composition (of treatises), the definition of Āyurveda —
notes: A list of the chapter's topics (nominatives), continued through v. 140, where they are summed up by "sarvam etat samākhyātam". "hetur āgamasya" can also be read together as "the cause of (its) coming", with "pravartanam" alone as "the propagation"; "āgama" means both "arrival" and "received (traditional) teaching". "sūtraṇa" = composing in sūtra form, i.e. writing the treatises.

words.gloss: effect, what is to be achieved

hindi: सम्पूर्ण कारण, कार्य, आयुर्वेद का प्रयोजन, हेतु (रोगों के कारण), दोष और औषध — संक्षेप में —
english: the complete (set of) cause(s), the effect, the purpose of Āyurveda; the causes (of disease), the doṣas, and medicine, in brief —
notes: Continues the topic list. "saṃpūrṇaṃ kāraṇam" = the complete cause; in the chapter this refers to the six categories (sāmānya, viśeṣa, guṇa, dravya, karma, samavāya), but the verse itself says only "complete cause". "hetavaḥ" = causes of disease (cf. the chapter's three causes); "saṃgraheṇa" (in brief) may qualify bheṣajam only or the whole list.

hindi: रस, (उनके) प्रत्यय-रूप द्रव्यों सहित; द्रव्यों का त्रिविध संग्रह (वर्गीकरण); मूलिनी, फलिनी, स्नेह और लवण —
english: the tastes (rasa) together with the substances that underlie them, the threefold classification of substances; the root-plants, the fruit-plants, the fats and the salts —
notes: "sapratyayadravyāḥ" (bahuvrīhi): "together with the substances that are their pratyaya (cause, basis)", referring to the chapter's account of the substrate of taste. pratyaya could also be rendered "cause" or "conditions". "trividho dravyasaṃgrahaḥ" refers to the chapter's threefold division of substances.

words.gloss: whose useful parts are latex and bark
merits and faults of proper and improper use

hindi: मूत्र, दूध (क्षीर) और वे छह वृक्ष जिनका आश्रय (उपयोगी अंग) दूध और छाल है; इन सबके कर्म; और उचित तथा अनुचित प्रयोग के गुण और दोष —
english: urine, the milks, and the six trees whose (useful parts) are latex and bark; the actions of all these; and the merits and faults of proper and improper application —
notes: "kṣīratvagāśrayāḥ" = "having latex and bark as their seat", parallel to "diṣṭapayastvacaḥ" in v. 119. "yogāyogaguṇāguṇāḥ" can be resolved as "the guṇas (merits) and aguṇas (faults) of yoga (proper use) and ayoga (improper use)", or as a four-member dvandva (proper use, improper use, merits, faults).
lines_iast: mūtraṃ kṣīrāṇi vṛkṣāśca ṣaḍ ye kṣīratvagāśrayāḥ
lines_deva: मूत्रं क्षीराणि वृक्षाश्च षड् ये क्षीरत्वगाश्रयाः

hindi: वैद्य की निन्दा (अर्थात् अयोग्य वैद्य की भर्त्सना) और (वह प्रसंग) जिसमें वैद्यों के सभी गुण स्थित हैं — यह सब महर्षि ने प्रथम अध्याय में भली-भाँति कहा है।
english: the censure of (unworthy) physicians, and (the passage) in which all the qualities of physicians are found — all this has been fully explained by the great sage in the first chapter.
notes: Closes the summary list begun in v. 136. "yatrasthāḥ ... guṇāḥ" is literally "the qualities ... which stand where"; it is taken as "(the section) in which all the physician's qualities are set out"; it may also be read loosely as "and all the qualities of physicians, as they are found (there)". "pūrvādhyāye" = literally "in the foremost/preceding chapter", i.e. this first chapter (an interpretation). The "great sage" is the teacher of the chapter (Ātreya), not named here. Alternatively yatra may refer to a person: '(the physician) in whom all the qualities of physicians reside' (cf. vv. 133-135); a reviewer reports commentators read it so, to be checked against Cakrapāṇi.
lines_iast: vaidyāpavādo yatrasthāḥ sarve ca bhiṣajāṃ guṇāḥ
lines_deva: वैद्यापवादो यत्रस्थाः सर्वे च भिषजां गुणाः
